Paper 2: 19th-century Novel and Poetry since 1789 — a core area of GCSE English Literature.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Paper 2: 19th-century Novel and Poetry since 1789 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Postmodernism just means literature written after modernism.
It means it is wrong to write fiction.
Postmodernism means writing about the future.
Self-aware metafiction, intertextuality, scepticism toward grand narratives, playfulness with form, and blurring of high/low culture.
Modernism is literature about modern technology like phones.
Experimentation with form (fragmentation, stream of consciousness), focus on subjective interior experience, scepticism toward traditional narrative and absolute truth.
Modernism just means literature written in modern times.
It means it is wrong to write fiction.
Modernism is literature about modern technology like phones.
It means authors can never make mistakes when writing.
It means it is wrong to write fiction.
The claim that judging a text by what the author 'intended' is fallacious — the text's meaning lies in the work itself, not the author's stated or guessed intentions.
